items.title: Perfect modules are exactly the modules with a finite projective resolution
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a module M over a ring R and proves the equivalence of two conditions: M is a perfect module, and there exists a resolution 0 -> F_d -> ... -> F_1 -> F_0 -> M -> 0 with each F_i finite projective (source lines 18916-18927). Part of the proof is immediate: assuming (2), the complex E^bullet with E^{-i} = F_i is quasi-isomorphic to M[0], hence M is perfect (proof lines 18930-18931). The substantive direction is (1) implies (2). By the perfect-complex statement and the statement on pseudo-coherence of modules, one can find a resolution E^bullet -> M with each E^{-i} finite free (proof lines 18932-18935). By the last-term-flat statement, the cokernel F_d = Coker(E^{d-1} -> E^d) is flat for d sufficiently large (proof lines 18936-18938). The Algebra statement on finitely presented flat modules then gives that F_d is finite projective (proof lines 18938-18940). The desired resolution is then the truncated one 0 -> F_d -> E^{-d+1} -> ... -> E^0 -> M -> 0 (proof lines 18941-18945). The non-routine content is the choice of d large enough that the cokernel becomes flat, which converts a possibly infinite free resolution into a finite projective one.
